title_tag: 10 Best Hotels in Dubai Marina (2026): Prices Compared
meta_description: Dubai Marina hotels from €95 to €257 a night compared on beach access, pools, breakfast cost and room size, so you pick the right tower, resort or suite.
h1_main: 10 Best Hotels in Dubai Marina in 2026
author_role: 10 Dubai Marina hotels compared on nightly price, guest score, room size, pool, beach and breakfast
lead: For most couples the Dubai Marina hotel to book is Grosvenor House at €236 a night: the highest guest score of the ten, 10 restaurants and free beach access at its sister resort. The best-value 5★ is InterContinental at €162 for a 43 m² room facing Dubai Marina Mall, families should look at JW Marriott (€257, kids' club), and the cheapest hotel is The First Collection at €96.

The catch most visitors miss: only one hotel here, the W at Mina Seyahi, is on the beach. The rest reach the sand on foot or by shuttle. All 10 were compared on price for the same night, guest and location score, pool and beach access, breakfast cost and room size. Filter by beach, suites, families, couples or budget below, or jump to the comparison table.

review: Grosvenor House is the one to book for a first trip to Dubai Marina. For €236 a night you get the page's top guest score (9.5) and a position on the Marina promenade, plus something no other tower hotel here matches: full use of the beach, pools and leisure facilities at Le Royal Meridien Beach Resort & Spa, with a free shuttle there and back.

Inside, it is the most complete package on the list: 10 restaurants (Buddha-Bar, Toro Toro, Rhodes W1, Indego by Vineet), Bar 44 on the top floor, two spas, two heated outdoor pools with a pool bar, and butler service. Bathrooms are marble with a soaking tub, rain shower and Byredo amenities.

Compared with JW Marriott (#3), it costs €21 less, starts check-in an hour earlier (14:00) and adds the beach deal, but JW has a kids' club and a direct mall link. Compared with the W (#4), you trade a beachfront address for a calmer hotel and a higher score.
The catch: the cheapest Deluxe Room is 377 ft² (about 35 m²), and taxes come on top (5% VAT, 7% municipality fee and an AED 20 tourism fee per night). Breakfast-included rates start at €285.

review: InterContinental is the value pick among the Marina's big 5★ hotels. €162 a night buys a 463 ft² Classic King Room (about 43 m²), bigger than the cheapest rooms at Grosvenor House (377 ft²) or JW Marriott (431 ft²), which cost €74 and €95 more.

The location is right in the middle of things: facing Dubai Marina Mall on the promenade, with easy access to the Dubai Tram and Jumeirah Beach. It has 328 rooms, an outdoor pool with pool bar, a separate kids' pool, a spa with 6 treatment suites and a Pilates studio, and four bars and restaurants including the rooftop Rex Bar in winter.

Breakfast is the other reason it wins on value: €20 to add, against €33 at the W and €36 at JW Marriott. If you want breakfast and flexibility, the free-cancellation breakfast rate is €219 and you pay nothing upfront.
What it lacks is a beach. There is no beach club or shuttle in the listing, so plan on a taxi or tram to Jumeirah Beach, or pick Grosvenor House if a daily beach day is non-negotiable.

review: JW Marriott is the family hotel of the Marina. It is one of two hotels here with a kids' club (Ciel is the other) and the only one that spells out the programme (PlayStation, climbing walls, toys, arts and crafts, a daily schedule of films, storytelling, dance and music), and it pairs that with a heated infinity pool on level 4 and a separate children's pool.

The other big draw is the direct link to Dubai Marina Mall and Marina Walk, which makes rainy-day or late-evening plans easy with children. The beach is a 5-minute stroll. Guests give it 9.4 overall and 9.6 for location.

At €257 a night it is the most expensive hotel on this page, and breakfast adds €36. The cheapest Deluxe City View Room is 431 ft² (about 40 m²) with a balcony and walk-in shower. A breakfast-included rate with free cancellation starts at €315.
One real catch for young families: the hotel lists no cots. With a baby, book the Marriott Harbour suites (#6) or Jumeirah Living (#8) instead.

review: If your Marina stay is really a beach holiday, this is the one to book. W Dubai Mina Seyahi sits at the Marina's western edge on the Jumeirah Beach coastline and is the only beachfront hotel on this list. Mina Seyahi Beach is 400 m away and Marina Beach less than 1 km.

For €248 a night the cheapest room is also the biggest standard room here: a 570 ft² Deluxe King with harbour view, balcony, bath and walk-in shower. That is €9 less than JW Marriott for 139 ft² more.

It is a social resort first. The infinity pool looks over Palm Jumeirah, the WET Deck at Ginger Moon runs live entertainment, and there are 7 venues including ATTIKO, Bussola and Fish Beach Taverna. It is also the only hotel here selling all-inclusive rates (from €471 for two).
The trade-off shows in the scores: 8.6 overall and 8.6 for location, the joint-lowest score and the lowest location mark of the ten. Pick Grosvenor House if you want a beach day without the party.

review: Ciel is the hotel you book for the view. It is sold as the world's tallest hotel, and the cheapest Deluxe King Room is €191 a night on a deal rate (30% off the usual price), €45 less than Grosvenor House and €66 less than JW Marriott.

What you get is height and facilities: three pools (outdoor, rooftop and infinity), 8 restaurants and lounges including Tattu Sky Lounge, Nuage and Koi House, a spa with sauna, a kids' club and an indoor play area. Accessibility is among the best here, with a dedicated 484 ft² disability-access room.

The trade-off is space. The Deluxe King is 291 ft² (about 27 m²), the joint-smallest cheapest room on this page with Vida, which works out at about €7 per m² against €3.80 at InterContinental. Premium King rooms (334 ft²) start at €248.
Barasti Beach is an 8-minute walk and The Walk at JBR 1.9 km, so beach days are easy without a shuttle.

review: This is the best deal on the page if you measure in square metres. For €236 a night you get a renovated 1,292 ft² One-Bedroom Suite (about 120 m²): a separate bedroom, a living room, a full kitchen with dishwasher and washing machine, and a private balcony. That is more than three times the floor space of Grosvenor House's €236 room.
The lowest rate also includes breakfast and free cancellation, which no other hotel on this list does at its card price. Breakfast is otherwise €29.

Facilities are hotel-grade: a heated outdoor pool, a spa with hot tub and sauna, a gym and four places to eat. The Observatory Grill Room & Bar on top has 360° views over Dubai Marina and Palm Jumeirah. Guests score it 9.4, with 9.8 for staff.

Catches: Wi-Fi scores only 7.9, the score rests on a small number of reviews, and children pay as adults from 6. For two-bedroom suites (1,722 ft², from €295) the tourism fee doubles to AED 30 a night.

review: Vida is the best 4★ in Dubai Marina for couples. €173 a night buys a City View Deluxe Room with a private balcony, and guests score the hotel 9.2 with 9.6 for location, joint highest on the page, ahead of several 5★ towers that cost more.

It is calmer than the big brands: one all-day restaurant (Origins), a bar, a year-round outdoor pool, a hot tub, a gym and soundproof rooms. The card rate comes with free cancellation and no prepayment.

Compared with Ciel (#5), the room is the same 291 ft² and €18 cheaper, with a balcony but without the rooftop pools. Compared with InterContinental (#2), it is €11 more for a much smaller room, so pick Vida for the balcony and the guest scores rather than space.
It is also one of three hotels here that accept pets (charges may apply). There are no extra beds, so families of three or four should look at the suites further down.

For families it has the most generous child policy on this page: free cots up to 3 and free extra beds up to 11. Add a 23-metre temperature-controlled infinity pool with Marina views, a kids' pool and a recreation area, and it beats JW Marriott (#3) for anyone with a baby.

Compared with the Marriott Harbour suites (#6), it costs €4 more for about half the space, and breakfast is extra (€22). What you pay for is the Jumeirah name, the service and the infinity pool. Metro, tram and water taxis are about 1 km away.
It is quiet by design: one lounge, and quiet hours from 22:00 to 07:00.

guide.h2: Dubai Marina Hotels Compared: Price, Score, Room Size and Beach
guide.html:
All ten prices are the lowest nightly rate for two adults on the same January weeknight, before taxes. Three of them (Ciel, Vida and The First Collection) were limited-time deal rates that night, so expect those three to cost more once the deal ends. The column that changes the picture is room size: the cheapest stays give you the most space: City Premiere's €95 apartment is twice the size of JW Marriott's €257 room, and The First Collection's €96 suite is bigger than every 5★ hotel room on the list except the W's 53 m² room.

guide.h2: Which Dubai Marina Hotel Should You Book?
guide.html:
• Best all-round, couples: #1 Grosvenor House, €236. Top score (9.5), 10 restaurants and free beach access at Le Royal Meridien.
  • 5★ on a budget: #2 InterContinental, €162, with a 43 m² room and €20 breakfast.
  • Families with kids over 2: #3 JW Marriott, €257, for the kids' club and the mall link. With a baby: #8 Jumeirah Living, €240 (free cots and extra beds up to 11).
  • Beach holiday: #4 W Mina Seyahi, €248, the only beachfront hotel here.
  • The view: #5 Ciel, €191, the world's tallest hotel with a rooftop pool.
  • Space and longer stays: #6 Marriott Harbour, €236 for a 120 m² suite with breakfast, or #10 City Premiere, €95 for an 83 m² apartment.
  • Cheapest hotel: #9 The First Collection, €96, with a rooftop pool and beach-club access.
  • Travelling with a pet: #7 Vida, €173, Jumeirah Living or the W.

Weighing the Marina against other areas? Our JBR hotels comparison covers the beachfront strip next door, and Palm Jumeirah hotels are the step up to private-beach resorts. If you want sand outside every room, see the best beach resorts in Dubai.

guide.h2: Staying in Dubai Marina: Where, Getting Around and Extra Costs
guide.html:
Which part of the Marina

  • Marina promenade and Dubai Marina Mall (Grosvenor House, InterContinental, JW Marriott): location scores 9.3–9.6, with the mall on foot (JW Marriott is linked to it directly). Vida and Marriott Harbour score 9.6 and 9.5.
  • Marina Gate and the JBR end (Jumeirah Living, Ciel): towers under 1–2 km from The Walk at JBR; Ciel is 8 minutes' walk from Barasti Beach.
  • Mina Seyahi (W): the Marina's beach edge, the only true beachfront address here, with the lowest location score (8.6).
  • Budget blocks (City Premiere, 750 m from Dubai Marina Metro; The First Collection on Al Seba Street): bigger units for less money; Hidden Beach is a 17-minute walk from The First Collection.

Getting around

Dubai Marina Metro Station is 750 m from City Premiere, and Jumeirah Living has metro, tram and water taxi stations about 1 km away. InterContinental has easy access to the Dubai Tram. Grosvenor House puts Dubai International at about 20 minutes by taxi; most other hotels list Al Maktoum International at 21–27 km. Parking is free at nine of the ten.

What costs extra

  • Taxes and fees: the room prices above exclude taxes and charges. Where the rates break them down, a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and a Dubai tourism fee of AED 15–20 per room per night are added (AED 30 on Marriott Harbour's two-bedroom suites).
  • Breakfast: €20 (InterContinental), €22 (Jumeirah Living), €29 (Marriott Harbour), €33 (W), €36 (JW Marriott). Only Marriott Harbour includes it at the lowest price.
  • Beach: free at the W (beachfront) and through Grosvenor House's sister resort; The First Collection lists a private beach area and free shuttle. Elsewhere you walk or taxi to a public beach.
  • Extra beds: from AED 100 (InterContinental, Marriott Harbour) to AED 360 (Grosvenor House) a night; free for under-12s at Jumeirah Living; not available at Vida.

When to go

The rates here are for mid-January, the cooler winter season when the pools, rooftop bars and beach clubs are at their best. The Marina is also the starting point for many boat trips: compare Dubai dinner cruises and jet ski tours if you want to see the skyline from the water.

The Marina is also where most boat trips leave from: our Dubai boat tours compared puts 10 speedboat and shared yacht cruises side by side on price per hour, route and departure point.

faqs.q: What is the best hotel in Dubai Marina?
faqs.a: Grosvenor House, a Luxury Collection Hotel, from €236 a night. It has the highest guest score of the ten compared (9.5), 10 restaurants and free beach and pool access at its sister resort Le Royal Meridien with a shuttle. For a beachfront room, pick W Dubai Mina Seyahi (€248).

faqs.q: How much does a hotel in Dubai Marina cost per night?
faqs.a: On a January weeknight for two adults, the ten options here ran from €95 (City Premiere, a one-bedroom apartment) to €257 (JW Marriott). The median was about €214. Taxes, VAT and a Dubai tourism fee of AED 15–20 per room per night come on top.

faqs.q: Do Dubai Marina hotels have a private beach?
faqs.a: Mostly not. Of the ten compared, only W Dubai Mina Seyahi is beachfront. Grosvenor House includes free beach access at Le Royal Meridien with a shuttle, and The First Collection lists a private beach area and free shuttle. JW Marriott is a 5-minute stroll from the beach and Ciel 8 minutes from Barasti Beach. For resorts with sand outside, see our Dubai beach resorts.

faqs.q: Is it better to stay in Dubai Marina or JBR?
faqs.a: Stay in the Marina for the promenade, the mall, and the metro (5★ hotels from €162 here); stay at JBR if you want to step straight onto the beach. Compare both with our best hotels in JBR.

faqs.q: Which Dubai Marina hotel is best for families?
faqs.a: JW Marriott Hotel Marina for kids over 2 (kids' club, children's pool, direct link to Dubai Marina Mall), and Jumeirah Living Marina Gate for babies and young children (free cots up to 3, free extra beds up to 11, kids' pool). For more space, the Marriott Harbour one-bedroom suite is 120 m² with breakfast for €236. More options in our Dubai family resorts guide.

faqs.q: Which Dubai Marina hotels allow pets?
faqs.a: Vida Dubai Marina & Yacht Club, Jumeirah Living Marina Gate and W Dubai Mina Seyahi accept pets; charges may apply. The other seven hotels on this list do not.

faqs.q: Are there apartments or suites in Dubai Marina for longer stays?
faqs.a: Yes. City Premiere has 83 m² one-bedroom apartments from €95, Dubai Marriott Harbour 120 m² one-bedroom suites with breakfast from €236, and Jumeirah Living 57 m² studios from €240. All three have a kitchen and a washing machine.

methodology: We compared 16 Dubai Marina hotels and apartment buildings on live prices for the same night (two adults, one night in mid-January) and kept the 10 that give a genuinely different choice: beach resort, tower hotel, suites and serviced apartments, from €95 to €257. Each was scored on the nightly price, guest score and location score, the size of the cheapest room, pools and beach access, breakfast cost, child and pet policies, and distances to the metro, mall and beach. Rankings reward the best all-round stay first, then the clearest pick for each type of traveller.
